steps: Identify which calculation: gas volume, atom economy, or percentage yield
For gas volume: find moles of gas (from equation), then multiply by 24
For atom economy: find Mr of desired product ÷ Mr of ALL products × 100
For yield: actual mass ÷ theoretical mass × 100
method_card.title: Gas Volumes and Atom Economy
method_card.content:
Three calculations that test different ideas.

Gas volume at RTP: one mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³ (24,000 cm³). Volume = moles × 24; moles = volume ÷ 24.

Atom economy is about the balanced equation: Mr of the desired product ÷ Mr of all products × 100. Use product Mr values, never reactants, and include the coefficients.

Percentage yield is about the experiment: actual ÷ theoretical × 100. It is always below 100% because of losses and side reactions.

exam_context.frequency: High : atom economy and gas volumes are common in Separate Chemistry

gold.display: 3.25 g of zinc reacts with excess HCl: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. The student collects 960 cm³ of hydrogen at RTP. Calculate the percentage yield. (Ar: Zn = 65)

misconceptions.message: Match the units before dividing: theoretical volume is 1.2 dm³ = 1200 cm³. Yield = (960 ÷ 1200) × 100 = 80%.
Put the actual amount on top: (960 ÷ 1200) × 100 = 80%, not (1200 ÷ 960) × 100.

gold.hint: Find the theoretical volume of H₂, convert to cm³, then compare with 960 cm³.

guided_steps.say: Find the theoretical volume of H₂, convert it to cm³, then compare with the 960 cm³ collected.

guided_steps.pre: convert to cm³ to match the data: 1.2 × 1000 =

guided_steps.done: Matches the 960 cm³ collected, so 80%.

gold.display: Two routes can produce calcium oxide (CaO). Route A: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ (Mr: CaO = 56, CO₂ = 44). Route B: Ca(OH)₂ → CaO + H₂O (Mr: CaO = 56, H₂O = 18). Calculate the atom economy for Route B. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

misconceptions.message: This is Route B (Ca(OH)₂ → CaO + H₂O): AE = 56 ÷ 74 × 100 = 75.7%. Route A would give 56%.
The desired product is CaO (56), not H₂O (18). AE = 56 ÷ 74 × 100 = 75.7%.

gold.hint: Route B has two products: add their Mr, then divide 56 by the total.

guided_steps.say: Route B is Ca(OH)₂ → CaO + H₂O. Atom economy uses the two products.

guided_steps.done: About a quarter is waste water; to 1 decimal place the atom economy is 75.7%.

gold.display: 32 g of iron(III) oxide reacts with carbon monoxide: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. Calculate the volume of CO₂ produced at RTP. (Mr: Fe₂O₃ = 160)

misconceptions.message: One Fe₂O₃ makes three CO₂, so moles CO₂ = 0.2 × 3 = 0.6. Volume = 0.6 × 24 = 14.4 dm³.

gold.hint: Find moles of Fe₂O₃, multiply by 3 for CO₂, then multiply by 24.

guided_steps.say: Find moles of Fe₂O₃, scale by the 1 : 3 ratio to CO₂, then multiply by 24.

guided_steps.done: Returns 0.6 mol CO₂, so 14.4 dm³.

gold.display: 12.25 g of potassium chlorate decomposes: 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂. Calculate the volume of oxygen produced at RTP. (Ar: K = 39, Cl = 35.5, O = 16)

misconceptions.message: The ratio 2KClO₃ : 3O₂ gives moles O₂ = 0.1 × 3 ÷ 2 = 0.15. Volume = 0.15 × 24 = 3.6 dm³.

gold.hint: Find Mr of KClO₃, then moles, then the 2:3 ratio to O₂, then multiply by 24.

guided_steps.say: Find Mr of KClO₃, then moles, then the 2 : 3 ratio, then multiply by 24.

guided_steps.done: Returns 0.15 mol O₂, so 3.6 dm³.

gold.display: 2.5 g of CaCO₃ reacts with excess HCl: CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂. The student collects 504 cm³ of CO₂ at RTP. Calculate the percentage yield. (Mr: CaCO₃ = 100)

misconceptions.message: Match the units: theoretical volume is 0.6 dm³ = 600 cm³. Yield = (504 ÷ 600) × 100 = 84%.
Put the actual amount on top: (504 ÷ 600) × 100 = 84%, not (600 ÷ 504) × 100.

gold.hint: Find the theoretical volume of CO₂ in cm³, then compare with 504 cm³.

guided_steps.say: Find the theoretical volume of CO₂ in cm³, then compare with the 504 cm³ collected.

guided_steps.done: Matches the 504 cm³ collected, so 84%.

gold.display: In the decomposition 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂, the desired product is oxygen. Calculate the atom economy. (Ar: K = 39, Cl = 35.5, O = 16)

misconceptions.message: Include the coefficients: 3O₂ (Mr 96) and 2KCl (Mr 149), total 245. Atom economy = 96 ÷ 245 × 100 = 39.2%.

gold.hint: Use the Mr of every product with its coefficient, then divide 96 by the total.

guided_steps.say: Oxygen is the desired product. Include the coefficients: 3O₂ and 2KCl.

guided_steps.done: About 61% is waste KCl; to 1 decimal place the atom economy is 39.2%.

bronze.display: Calculate the volume occupied by 0.5 mol of hydrogen gas at RTP. Give your answer in dm³.

misconceptions.message: Multiply by 24, don't divide. Volume = moles × 24 = 0.5 × 24 = 12 dm³.

guided_steps.say: At RTP one mole of any gas fills 24 dm³, so volume = moles × 24.

guided_steps.hint: Divide back by the molar volume.
guided_steps.done: Returns our 0.5 mol, so the volume is 12 dm³.

bronze.display: A gas has a volume of 4.8 dm³ at RTP. Calculate the number of moles of gas.

misconceptions.message: Moles = volume ÷ 24 = 4.8 ÷ 24 = 0.2 mol. Divide, don't multiply.

guided_steps.say: Volume is given and moles are wanted, so divide: moles = volume ÷ 24.

guided_steps.done: Returns 4.8 dm³, so 0.2 mol is right.

bronze.display: Calculate the volume of 2 mol of oxygen gas at RTP in dm³.

misconceptions.message: Volume = moles × 24 = 2 × 24 = 48 dm³. Multiply, don't divide.

guided_steps.say: At RTP volume = moles × 24.

guided_steps.done: Returns 2 mol, so 48 dm³ is right.

bronze.display: In the reaction CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂, the only desired product is CaO. Calculate the atom economy. (Mr: CaO = 56, CO₂ = 44)
bronze.equation_hint: \(\text{atom economy} = \frac{M_r \text{ of desired product}}{M_r \text{ of all products}} \times 100\)

misconceptions.message: The desired product is CaO (Mr 56), not CO₂. Atom economy = 56 ÷ (56 + 44) × 100 = 56%.

bronze.hint: Add the two product Mr values for the denominator, then divide 56 by it.

guided_steps.say: Atom economy = \(M_r\) of desired product ÷ \(M_r\) of all products × 100.

guided_steps.done: 44 g of every 100 is wasted as CO₂, so atom economy is 56%.

bronze.display: In the reaction 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO, the desired product is MgO. Calculate the atom economy.
bronze.equation_hint: \(\text{atom economy} = \frac{M_r \text{ of desired product}}{M_r \text{ of all products}} \times 100\)

misconceptions.message: O₂ is a reactant, not a product. The only product is MgO, so atom economy = 100%.

bronze.hint: With only one product, every atom ends up where you want it.

guided_steps.say: Atom economy = \(M_r\) of desired product ÷ \(M_r\) of all products × 100.

guided_steps.pre: How many products are there in 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO?
guided_steps.hint: Count what is right of the arrow.

guided_steps.pre: With one product every atom is wanted: (all ÷ all) × 100 =
guided_steps.hint: Anything divided by itself is 1, times 100.

guided_steps.done: No waste at all, so atom economy is 100%.

bronze.display: A student expected to make 10 g of a salt but only obtained 7.5 g. Calculate the percentage yield.

misconceptions.message: Yield = actual ÷ theoretical × 100 = (7.5 ÷ 10) × 100 = 75%. Actual goes on top.

bronze.hint: Put actual over theoretical, then times 100.

guided_steps.say: Percentage yield = actual ÷ theoretical × 100.

guided_steps.hint: The amount you expected to make.

guided_steps.done: Matches the 7.5 g actually made, so 75%.

bronze.display: In the reaction 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂, 0.1 mol of H₂O₂ decomposes. Calculate the volume of O₂ produced at RTP in dm³.

misconceptions.message: From 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂, 2 mol H₂O₂ give 1 mol O₂, so 0.1 mol H₂O₂ gives 0.05 mol O₂. Volume = 0.05 × 24 = 1.2 dm³.

bronze.hint: Halve the H₂O₂ moles for O₂, then multiply by 24.

guided_steps.say: Use the equation ratio to find moles of O₂, then multiply by 24.

guided_steps.pre: moles of H₂O₂ per mole of O₂ in 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂ =
guided_steps.hint: Coefficient of H₂O₂ over coefficient of O₂.

guided_steps.done: Returns 0.05 mol O₂, so 1.2 dm³.

bronze.display: A gas occupies 7.2 dm³ at RTP. Calculate the number of moles of gas.

misconceptions.message: Moles = volume ÷ 24 = 7.2 ÷ 24 = 0.3 mol. Divide, don't multiply.

guided_steps.say: Moles are wanted from a volume, so divide by 24.

guided_steps.done: Returns 7.2 dm³, so 0.3 mol.

silver.display: 5.0 g of calcium carbonate decomposes: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Calculate the volume of CO₂ produced at RTP in dm³. (Mr: CaCO₃ = 100)

misconceptions.message: Find moles first: 5.0 ÷ 100 = 0.05. Volume = 0.05 × 24 = 1.2 dm³. Do not multiply the mass by 24.

silver.hint: Find moles from the mass, then multiply by 24.

guided_steps.say: Mass is given, so find moles first, then use the 1 : 1 ratio, then multiply by 24.

guided_steps.done: Returns 0.05 mol, so 1.2 dm³ of CO₂.

silver.display: 4.6 g of sodium reacts with water: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. Calculate the volume of hydrogen gas produced at RTP in dm³. (Ar: Na = 23)

misconceptions.message: 2 mol Na make 1 mol H₂, so halve: moles H₂ = 0.2 ÷ 2 = 0.1. Volume = 0.1 × 24 = 2.4 dm³.

silver.hint: Moles of Na, then halve for H₂, then multiply by 24.

guided_steps.say: Find moles of Na, then use the 2 : 1 ratio, then multiply by 24.

guided_steps.hint: Two Na make one H₂, so halve.

guided_steps.done: Returns 0.1 mol H₂, so 2.4 dm³.

silver.display: 0.6 g of magnesium reacts with excess HCl: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. Calculate the volume of hydrogen produced at RTP in dm³. (Ar: Mg = 24)

misconceptions.message: Find moles first: 0.6 ÷ 24 = 0.025. Volume = 0.025 × 24 = 0.6 dm³. Do not multiply the mass by 24.

silver.hint: Find moles from the mass, ratio 1:1, then multiply by 24.

guided_steps.say: Find moles of Mg first, ratio 1 : 1 with H₂, then multiply by 24.

guided_steps.done: Returns 0.025 mol, so 0.6 dm³.

silver.display: 10 g of iron(III) oxide is reduced: 2Fe₂O₃ + 3C → 4Fe + 3CO₂. The student obtains 5.6 g of iron. Calculate the percentage yield. (Mr: Fe₂O₃ = 160, Ar: Fe = 56)

misconceptions.message: The ratio 2Fe₂O₃ : 4Fe is 1 : 2, so moles Fe = 0.125 and theoretical mass = 7.0 g. Yield = (5.6 ÷ 7.0) × 100 = 80%.

silver.hint: Find the theoretical mass of iron, then actual over theoretical times 100.

guided_steps.say: Find the theoretical mass of iron, then compare it with the 5.6 g actually made.

guided_steps.done: Matches the 5.6 g made, so 80%.

silver.display: In the reaction Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂, the desired product is iron. Calculate the atom economy. (Mr: Fe = 56, CO₂ = 44)
silver.equation_hint: \(\text{atom economy} = \frac{M_r \text{ of desired}}{M_r \text{ of all products}} \times 100\)

misconceptions.message: Include the coefficients: 2Fe (Mr 112) and 3CO₂ (Mr 132). Atom economy = 112 ÷ 244 × 100 = 45.9%.

silver.hint: Use the Mr of every product with its coefficient, then divide 112 by the total.

guided_steps.say: Atom economy uses the \(M_r\) of every product, coefficients included.

guided_steps.done: About 54% of the product mass is waste CO₂, so atom economy is 45.9%.

silver.display: In the reaction N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, the desired product is ammonia. Calculate the atom economy.
silver.equation_hint: \(\text{atom economy} = \frac{M_r \text{ of desired}}{M_r \text{ of all products}} \times 100\)

misconceptions.message: NH₃ is the only product, so all atoms end up in it. Atom economy = 100%.

silver.hint: With only one product, every atom is wanted.

guided_steps.say: Atom economy = \(M_r\) of desired ÷ \(M_r\) of all products × 100.

guided_steps.hint: Count what is right of the arrow.

guided_steps.pre: One product means all atoms are wanted: (all ÷ all) × 100 =

guided_steps.done: No waste, so atom economy is 100%.

problem_bank.bronze_description: One equation with values already in the right units: molar volume, or atom economy where there is a single desired product.
problem_bank.silver_description: Convert a mass to moles, or use the equation's ratio, before the gas law, in one clean chain.
problem_bank.gold_description: Multi-step problems: a theoretical amount then percentage yield, unit conversions (dm³ to cm³), or atom economy with coefficients.

bronze.title: Bronze: one gas-law step
steps: Molar volume: at RTP one mole of any gas fills 24 dm³. Volume = moles × 24; moles = volume ÷ 24.
Atom economy for a single desired product = \(M_r\) of that product ÷ \(M_r\) of all products × 100.
Values arrive ready to use. Pick the equation, substitute, then state the unit (dm³, mol or %).

example.question: Calculate the volume of 3 mol of nitrogen gas at RTP, in dm³.

silver.title: Silver: convert to moles first
steps: A mass or a different substance is given, so find moles first: moles = mass ÷ \(M_r\).
Use the balanced equation's ratio to switch to the gas you want, then volume = moles × 24.
For yield, turn moles into a theoretical mass (moles × \(A_r\)), then actual ÷ theoretical × 100.

example.question: 6.0 g of carbon burns: C + O₂ → CO₂. Calculate the volume of CO₂ at RTP, in dm³. (Ar: C = 12)

gold.title: Gold: two ideas chained
steps: Multi-step: often a theoretical amount then a comparison, so plan the route before you start.
Watch units: molar volume gives dm³, but collected gas is often in cm³. 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³.
Atom economy needs the coefficients in every \(M_r\) (2Fe means 2 × 56). Round only at the very end.
